Checked on the sheet. A neat stack of cartoon logs that reads well as a log barrier. Squash it to 0.95 tall and stretch it to 2.0 wide for variety in the forest.

picks.why: Checked on the sheet. It shares the flat-shaded style of the first pick, with a picket variant for variety. The wood is quite dark, so it would benefit from a brighter tint. Skip index 1, which is a collider.

picks.what: blank low-poly wooden sign board with a short stub post
picks.why: Clean, cartoony low-poly signboard (44 tris) that clearly reads as a sign. Flip it upside down so the stub post becomes the hanger from the crossbeam, and scale it about 7x to roughly 2.0 x 1.0. Its style matches the rest of the village pack.
Hand-painted cartoon wood (92 tris) with the best stylized look. Scale its height up so it reads as a hanging plank board.
A warm hand-painted plank fits an enchanted forest and works like a fallen branch or log board to slide under. Very low tri count.
A simple trail-sign silhouette that reads clearly. Hang it upside down and scale it about 7x.
A stylized wooden plank suits a pirate dock. Scale it up into a weathered gangway or board sign.
A dark-wood sign board fits a dock tavern sign. It is very cheap (44 tris).
Dark wood reads well against snow and looks like a mountain trail sign. It is clean low-poly and cheap.
A stylized wooden plank as a backup that contrasts well with white snow.

picks.what: wooden crate stacked 2 high (2.0x2.0x2.0 per crate, scale depth to 1.6)

picks.what: red brick cube stretched to 2.9 tall
picks.why: Confirmed: a saturated red brick block, 2.0x2.0x2.1 at 1456 tris. Its solid box silhouette matches the hit volume exactly, and it is in the same kit as the crate.
Confirmed: a tall, chunky brown pillar, 2.6x3.0x3.1 at 576 tris. It is already close to 2.0x2.9 and gives a clear cartoon silhouette, in a style that is coherent with the platformer kit.

picks.what: single brown rock pillar / tree stump scaled to 2.9 tall
picks.why: Confirmed: a smooth, tapered stump at 288 tris that reads as a giant tree trunk. It matches the look of #31 and gives that piece some variety.

picks.what: giant cupcake scaled ~20x to 2.0 wide x 2.9 tall
picks.why: Confirmed: a cute pastel-purple cupcake with sprinkles and a chunky silhouette, the best fit for candy land. At 4368 tris it is slightly over the 4k budget, so decimate it a little. The tiramisu was rejected because it looks murky and semi-realistic, with a hollow ring-shaped outline in piece 0.
Confirmed: a hand-painted pirate crate at only 196 tris. It is the most readable box shape for a block on the dock and matches the harbor's pirate pack.

picks.what: pirate barrel, stacked 2x2 (or a crate with a barrel on top)
picks.why: Confirmed: a chunky hand-painted barrel at 504 tris, so a stack of 4 is about 2k tris. It comes from the same pack as the crate, which keeps one look across the dock.

picks.what: tall grey rock scaled to 2.0x2.9 (tint cooler / add white snow-cap material)

A cute statue that suits the biome, at about 4k tris in total. The model is split into 15 parts (body spheres, claws, carrot nose, gems), so use the whole model at -1. Its outline is irregular, so it is second choice behind the rock.

Checked on the sheet: a clean flat-shaded rectangular bale with a bulged middle, 56 tris and 1.6x1.4x1.1 in size, which is close to the hit volume. It reads instantly as hay, which suits a slot named hay. Scale it up a little and turn it to sit across the lane.
Checked on the sheet: a bright, smooth Clash-style crate with a crisp cube silhouette, 392 tris. It matches the warm cartoon look of the village and gives a non-hay variety block.
Checked on the sheet: 1.8x1.2x1.8 and 1082 tris, almost exactly the hit volume. It has a chunky, saturated cartoon wood look and reads clearly as a block to jump over in a forest.

picks.what: pair of cut tree stumps (one lying, one upright)

picks.what: cupcake with purple frosting and sprinkles

picks.what: single cube present box with patterned wrap

Checked on the sheet: a chunky hand-painted crate with 196 tris and a clear cube silhouette. Its pirate-pack style suits the dock. The wood is somewhat dark, so boost saturation slightly.

picks.what: wooden barrel with iron bands (lay on its side)

picks.what: long wooden cart with barrels (whole model)

verdicts.reason: Sheet confirms #42 is the short chunky brown picket fence (3.3x1.2x0.2, 440t). It is bold, saturated cartoon and reads instantly as a jump-over. Scaling it to 2.0x0.95 is a mild squash.

The index is correct (rustic rail/picket fence), but on the sheet it is spindly and crooked, with thin rails and mostly see-through gaps. At 0.3 deep it would read as a thin scribble at phone running speed and makes a weak jump cue next to the chunky Quaternius fence. #28 from the same kit as rank 1 is the same bold style with a longer picket run.

Sheet confirms #7 is a blank sign board on a stub post (44t). It reads clearly as a sign. Its texture is very dark, desaturated brown, much darker than the Quaternius and Clash-pack wood, so it needs a strong warm or bright tint, or a painted face or colour, to be seen against the road. Note that the pack's raw size is about 0.1 units, so it needs roughly a 20x scale, not 7x. The listed alternatives (old-medieval-sign-board, whose parts are mostly empty or a black frame; candy #13, a 0.2-tall thin realistic plank) are worse.

#1 is the hand-painted plank (8.1x1.2x0.4, 92t). It is already about 1.2 tall, so only its length needs compressing about 4x, which will squash the painted grain. It is dark and only acceptable as a backup. No better listed candidate exists.
#49 is the chunky X-braced cartoon crate, 2.0 cube, 264t. Stacked two high it is a clear, bright dodge block.
#12 is the saturated red brick cube (2.0x2.0x2.1, 1456t). It is a platformer-style block that matches the hit box and fits the kit. It is slightly less 'village', but it reads well.
#20 is the bulged golden hay bale (1.6x1.4x1.1, 56t). It is correct, readable and right-sized. Its flat-shaded pale tan should be pushed more yellow and saturated to match the Quaternius pieces.

#21 is the X-braced Clash-style crate (0.7 cube, 392t). It reads clearly and needs non-uniform scaling to 1.8x1.15x1.4. It is a second crate look next to the wall crate #49, but the two are close enough in style.

The sheet shows 35 loose parts (wheel, planks up to 9.9 long, staves, hoops) that assemble into a long barrel cart. It is the least-bad wooden 'long vehicle' for a village. Its texture is very dark, near-black brown, which clashes with the bright kit, so it needs a strong tint. The barrels make the roof bumpy, so it needs a flat collider. It is also listed as oncoming rank 2; don't reuse it there.

The sheet renders every part solid black. A 'gravity tram' is sci-fi and off-theme for a fairy-tale village. It is about 7.4k tris at 0.9 m raw size, so it needs a 10x stretch, and it is too heavy to repeat. The stagecoach is at least a period carriage; it is also dark and heavy (body+wheels+frame about 10k tris, which needs decimating or dropping the frame), but it fits the biome.
The sheet shows the cart body (#0) plus a pair of spoked wheels (#1), about 1.1k tris. It has a readable hand-cart silhouette. It is dark brown and needs a warm, bright tint.

This is the same model already used as trainCar rank 1. Showing it at 3.2 m as a charging cart and at 9 m as a rideable car is confusing in gameplay. It is also near-black. The Clash-style wooden cart #4 from the medieval env pack is bright and saturated, matches the barrel, crate and log picks, and is about 1.2k tris.
#11 is the bright banded Clash-style barrel, 1.2 cube, 758t. It is the right size and an obvious roller.

**Art style:** The core look comes from three packs: the Quaternius platformer kit (bold, saturated, glossy), the Clash-like medieval env pack (warm orange-brown flat colour) and the lowpoly-medieval-village pack (flat-shaded, slightly muted). Together they hold up as one cartoon style.

- **Spindly fence:** the medieval env #10 fence reads poorly at speed, so I rejected it in favour of platformer #28.

verified.styleNotes: Overall the forest set holds together well. Two flat-colour cartoon kits do most of the work: the glossy medieval environment pack (a85053) and Quaternius platformer (8e016b), with saturated greens and golden wood. Stop using the stacked logs (a85053 #5) for both lowbar and hay; use the platformer short picket fence (#42) for lowbar. The trainCar has no good forest candidate: the barrel cart is short, dark and has a curved barrel top, and the gravity tram renders as black sci-fi parts. Reuse another biome's flat-roof car or build a procedural log wagon. Several parts have off scales (trampoline at about 270 units, e440b9 at about 0.1), so normalise them by bounding box, not by the suggested multipliers. verified.styleNotes: Three source styles are mixed here. (a) The sweets pack is soft-shaded, textured and pastel-purple. (b) The platformer kit is smooth, chunky and cartoony, but its default colours are dull: brown, maroon, dark green, black. (c) The christmas-presents pack has dark, photo-like wrap textures. To make one coherent candy style: retint every platformer-kit piece (fence, crate, spikes, spring, spiked ball, mace, tree) to a shared pastel palette (pink, mint, cream, strawberry red, chocolate brown), and replace or flatten the present-box textures with solid pastel colours plus a ribbon tint. Cell 17 carries Hogwarts-style crests and must not ship. The tram is all-black, with materials missing on the sheet, and needs a full re-material. Mesh over-reuse is the main readability risk: the cupcake was used for wall, hay, drop and decorLarge, and the donut for rolling, bounce and decorLarge. Obstacle slots with different player responses (wall = dodge, hay = jump) must not share a silhouette, and hazard meshes should not also appear as roadside decor. All sweets-pack meshes are about 0.1 m in source and need about 10-30x scaling. The donut (6.9k) and cupcake (4.4k) need decimating for the obstacle budget.

verified.styleNotes:
I checked every index against its sheet and all of them match their descriptions. Seven sources are mixed here. Quaternius platformer is smooth and saturated. The medieval environment pack is bright orange cartoon wood. The pirate asset pack is dark hand-painted wood. The pirate island pack is muted and flat-textured. The barrel cart, wooden cart and stylized fence are dark brown. The trampoline is untextured. The zombie container is plain red. The biggest mismatch is the dark woods (pirate pack, stylized fence and both carts) next to the bright Quaternius and medieval props. Apply one shared tint or saturation boost, or lighten the dark textures toward warm orange-brown, so the dock reads as one style.

Readability fixes:
- Hay should not use the sideways pirate barrel, which would look identical to the rolling barrel.
- The open-top pirate crate #5 needs a lid wherever the camera can see its top.
- The highbar should not use the thin plank that the sweeper also uses.
- The barrel cart can't be both the trainCar and the oncoming vehicle, because players couldn't tell what is safe to ride on.

Geometry fixes:
- The container #30 is yawed about 45 degrees and must be re-oriented.
- The stylized-fence plank is modelled at a slant and must be levelled.
- The barrel cart is only shown as loose parts and includes a 9.3 m shaft. Render it assembled before using it as the oncoming vehicle.
- The trampoline is in cm.

Cell 54 is the correct grey boulder. A falling mountain rock is logical. It is also the hay rank 1, so a dropped rock looks like a static hay block, which is acceptable because the shadow warns first.

Cell 20 is the dark blue lidded box. Its photo-like mottled texture is darker and less cartoony than the kit, and it is in cm units (2.5 m raw), so rescale it. It reads as a present and is acceptable as a second pick. A brighter tint is recommended.
Cell 27 is the correct log. It needs about a 6.7x stretch along its length to reach 7.4 m, and the knot will smear, but a long log reads clearly as a sweeper.
Cell 35 is the red-capped coil spring. It is instantly readable as a bouncer and pops on snow.
The sheet shows a blue rim ring, a dark grey mat and thin wire legs in cm units (3 m). It is plain but readable. Rescale it and drop the legs to ground level.
Cell 24 is the bright tiered cartoon pine, the best snow tree. Frost the tiers.
Cell 11 is a flat-shaded tiered pine, which is correct and consistent.
Cell 14 is the slim cone pine, which is correct and gives good treeline variety.
Cell 7 is the dark castle tower with a red flag. It is cartoon-style and works as a landmark, though slightly spooky dark grey. Use it sparingly.
Cell 13 shows the brown stacked rock outcrops, which are correct. The brown reads more desert than snow, so add white tops as noted.

Cell 5 is a shaggy, olive, semi-realistic card-leaf pine. Its drooping alpha-like foliage clashes with the clean tiered cartoon pines already picked, and it is hard to frost convincingly. The stylized tiered pine is more consistent.
Its parts are verified as a cute snowman, an ideal snow prop. It is also the shifter, so tint or scale the decor copy differently, or players may flinch at roadside snowmen.
Cell 5 is the log pile, which suits the cabin. It is the same model as hay rank 2, which is a minor decor-versus-obstacle overlap that is acceptable off-track.
Cell 6 is the campfire ringed with stones, a nice warm accent that matches the pack style.

This is exactly the same model as lowbar rank 2. A jump obstacle reused 2-6 m off track at running speed on a phone teaches players to misread obstacles, and its near-black wood is the weakest-looking fence anyway. Replace it with a same-kit prop.
Cell 50 is the tall rock, which is correct. It is the same as wall rank 1, but large rocks beside the track read naturally as scenery. Use a smaller scale.
Cell 54 is the boulder, which is correct. It is the same as hay and drop, so keep it small (well below 1 m) for ground variety and avoid confusion.

verified.styleNotes: The core style comes from the Quaternius Ultimate Platformer pack (rocks, spikes, spring, spiked ball, mace, tower) plus the low-poly-medieval-environment pack (logs, pine, campfire) and the ec3ce5 flat-shaded pines. Together these form one coherent, chunky, smooth-shaded cartoon set. The outliers are as follows. The snowman-golem has drab, semi-realistic textures and is long and spider-like, so it is rejected for both wall and shifter. The free-pack-tree #5 is a shaggy semi-realistic pine, rejected. The 309cf2 cart is dark and gritty and is a single shafted cart, not a train car. It is kept only because the alternative (gravity-tram) renders untextured black, but a procedural or custom flat-roof wagon would be better. The Christmas present #20 and the hand-painted plank are texture-based, which is a mild mismatch, so brighten them. The fence picks are flat-shaded and dark, and they must be rotated 90 degrees because their long axis is Z. Several cm-unit models (presents, trampoline, deadca pine) need rescaling. Avoid reusing exact obstacle models as roadside decor (fence, boulder, snowman), or scale and tint the decor copies differently. Overall the palette is grey and brown on white, so add a snow-cap or white-top material and a few saturated accents (red spring, red spikes, campfire, red tower flag) to keep it from looking flat.
